I use Free Software exclusively unless there is no open alternative. Even though some proprietary programs might be more polished than their free software counterpart, I enjoy using the software more because typically (but not always) free software is built with user freedom and privacy as a high priority. Like anyone else I also make sure and keep all my software patched. I use and recommend many of the free software tools listed here.

I don't go to extreme lengths to hide myself online or to heavily encrypt my communications, as that would take up far too much time during my day. But I do make conscientious choices to use software, websites, or devices which I have looked into and overall feel confident has the best privacy respecting design or features. I generally avoid Google services, as an example, because their entire business model is collecting and selling user info for advertising purposes. But sometimes I absolutely can't find a business or location and am forced to use Google maps on my phone to navigate there. You just have to do the best you can sometimes. If I have the choice and the time, I'd prefer looking up my destination using OpenStreetMap instead.
